name: Rio de Janeiro
description: City surfing between granite peaks: Arpoador's sandbars, Barra's long beach and the wild coves of the west zone.

surf_spots.name: Arpoador
surf_spots.description: Sandbar peak wrapping off the Arpoador rock at the end of Ipanema. Rights and lefts, busy with locals at sunset.

surf_spots.name: Ipanema (Posto 9-10)
surf_spots.description: Gentle beach break on small swells, good for lessons. Gets closeouts when the swell is big.

surf_spots.name: Barra da Tijuca
surf_spots.description: Long open beach with many peaks along the Postos, so it's easy to find space. Picks up most S and SE swells.

surf_spots.name: Prainha
surf_spots.description: Rio's most consistent wave, in a nature reserve west of Recreio. Powerful rights and lefts, rips on big days.

surf_spots.name: Itacoatiara (Niteroi)
surf_spots.description: Heavy, hollow shorebreak across the bay in Niteroi. Experts and bodyboarders only.

destination_seasons.notes: Summer: small, crowded, hot. Surf early before the sea breeze.
Carnival crowds. Small swells, occasional E windswell.
First autumn S swells start to show.
Good season starts: cold fronts bring S swells and offshore mornings.
Prime time. Prainha and Arpoador at their best.
Most consistent month. Bring a 3/2 wetsuit for dawn.
Big S swells; Itacoatiara wakes up. Coolest water of the year.
Swells easing; NE wind more frequent in the afternoon.
Spring: mixed swells, wind is the main issue. Surf mornings.
Late-season S swells still show up between fronts. Barra and Arpoador are the safest bets; surf before 10am.
Summer holidays: small and crowded. Mornings and longboards.
